record.paper_title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
record.original_question: Determine whether reverse-mathematical strengths for big Ramsey structures differ for homogeneous structures whose big Ramsey degrees are not simply characterized, such as the triangle-free homogeneous graph or the generic partial order, compared with the rationals and the Rado graph.

evidence.quote: Computability-theoretic and reverse mathematical aspects have been investigated by Anglès d’Auriac, Cholak, Dzhafarov, Monin, and Patey.

As these structures both have simply characterized big Ramsey degrees, it will be interesting to see if different reverse mathematical strengths emerge for structures such as the triangle-free homogeneous graph or the generic partial order.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For a countable homogeneous relational structure $\mathcal{M}$ and a finite substructure $A \subseteq \mathcal{M}$, the big Ramsey degree of $A$ in $\mathcal{M}$ is the least integer $T(A,\mathcal{M})$ (if it exists) such that for every finite coloring of the copies of $A$ in $\mathcal{M}$, there is an isomorphic copy $\mathcal{M}' \subseteq \mathcal{M}$ of $\mathcal{M}$ in which the copies of $A$ take at most $T(A,\mathcal{M})$ colors. A "big Ramsey structure" for $\mathcal{M}$ is an expansion of $\mathcal{M}$ that encodes these degrees via canonical partitions.

For $\mathcal{M}$ either the rational linear order $(\mathbb{Q},<)$ or the Rado graph $\mathcal{R}$, the big Ramsey degrees admit simple closed-form characterizations (à la Devlin and Laflamme–Sauer–Vuksanović), and the reverse-mathematical strengths of the corresponding big Ramsey theorems have been analyzed within subsystems of second-order arithmetic (such as $\mathrm{RCA}_0$, $\mathrm{WKL}_0$, $\mathrm{ACA}_0$, $\mathrm{ACA}_0'$, $\mathrm{ATR}_0$).

By contrast, the universal homogeneous triangle-free graph $\mathcal{H}_3$ (the Henson graph) and the generic countable partial order $\mathcal{P}$ have big Ramsey degrees whose known characterizations are intricate (using diagonal antichains of coding trees in the triangle-free case, and parameter-space / Carlson–Simpson methods in the partial-order case) and are not "simply characterized" in the above sense.

Problem. Determine the reverse-mathematical strengths of the statements
\[ \mathrm{BRD}(\mathcal{H}_3): \text{ every finite substructure of } \mathcal{H}_3 \text{ has a finite big Ramsey degree in } \mathcal{H}_3, \]
\[ \mathrm{BRD}(\mathcal{P}): \text{ every finite substructure of } \mathcal{P} \text{ has a finite big Ramsey degree in } \mathcal{P}, \]
over $\mathrm{RCA}_0$, and decide whether these strengths differ from those of the analogous statements for $(\mathbb{Q},<)$ and for the Rado graph $\mathcal{R}$. In particular, exhibit subsystems of second-order arithmetic to which $\mathrm{BRD}(\mathcal{H}_3)$ and $\mathrm{BRD}(\mathcal{P})$ are equivalent over $\mathrm{RCA}_0$, and compare them with the known strengths for $(\mathbb{Q},<)$ and $\mathcal{R}$.
artifact.category_tag: Reverse mathematics of big Ramsey degrees
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers (2021–2025) on big Ramsey degrees note that while reverse-mathematical analyses have been carried out for $(\mathbb{Q},<)$ and the Rado graph (work of Anglès d'Auriac, Cholak, Dzhafarov, Monin, Patey), the analogous reverse-mathematical strengths for the universal homogeneous triangle-free graph and the generic partial order remain to be determined. No publication explicitly settling the comparison has been located, so the problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: As these structures both have simply characterized big Ramsey degrees, it will be interesting to see if different reverse mathematical strengths emerge for structures such as the triangle-free homogeneous graph or the generic partial order.
status_evidence.claim: The question of reverse-mathematical strengths for these structures is raised as open.

status_evidence.title: Characterisation of the big Ramsey degrees of the generic partial order
status_evidence.snippet: Big Ramsey degrees of the generic partial order are characterized using parameter spaces and the Carlson–Simpson theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization exists but is not 'simply characterized' as in the Q or Rado case.

status_evidence.title: The Ramsey theory of the universal homogeneous triangle-free graph Part II
status_evidence.snippet: Exact big Ramsey degrees of the triangle-free Henson graph are computed via coding tree methods.
status_evidence.claim: Big Ramsey degrees for the Henson graph are known but their reverse-mathematical strength is not.
